reply_text:
㊥ ("what is needed to see this working") A demo exists the moment one thing is built that nobody has built yet: a resume brief in the agent's first prompt. Everything the brief reads is now stored. The classifier improves the brief; it does not gate it. And on session end, you are right, and I will say so plainly below. Let me ground one claim first: whether a conversation can be joined across sessions from what the records already carry.㊢ (checked, and a correction of my own earlier claim) The turn records carry no mission or excursion field at all, across 3,735 records. The join I named two evenings ago, "every chat turn carries its clocked target", is not on the records; the mission id lives on the roster per seat (15 seats on M-象-2000 right now) and would have to be stamped onto each record at write time. I could not reach the evidence query route to check the chat-turn evidence either. So the first thing a demo needs is a one-field change: the turn service writes the seat's mission id onto the record. Without it there is no conversation, only sessions.

🈖 ("what is needed to see this working") Your acceptance sense was: jumping into an agent chat feels like continuing a familiar conversation. The demo that shows it is a resume brief placed in the agent's first prompt, and then you ask something and watch whether it re-asks. Four pieces, three of them small:
1. **Mission id on the record** (above). Then "conversation" is classical: all records whose seat was on M-X, across sessions and agents.
2. **A brief generator**, classical, reading the fields that went live yesterday: open ports with their witness or "no answer linked", standings in force, obligations, plus minus40's facts about the mission's entities with referent dates, plus the operator-voice anchor from the mission file. No model.
3. **Delivery**: an Emacs command that inserts the brief at the top of a fresh REPL buffer, or the session-mode hook that composes the first prompt. Either is a few lines on the voxterm/session-mode side.
4. **The measure**: count of re-asks in the first turn after resume, over real resumes. It can fail.
The classifier is not on this path. It makes the brief more honest about "answered" against "addressed, still owed", which is the 368-of-758 finding; the brief can show the witness and let you judge until then.

㊣ ("lots has been done without any interactive demo") Agreed, and it is the pattern of the last three days: the record side was built to the spec and checked by recompute totals, and nobody has yet looked at it as a user. The inbox page is a ten-minute rebuild, not a thing you sit in front of. The brief is the first artifact that puts the stored state in front of a reader at the moment it matters.

㊣ ("would an 'end' really be needed") No, and the reason is the same unit problem. Lapsed and orphaned presume that the session is the conversation: an agent port lapses because that agent's session is gone, an operator ask is orphaned because nobody in that session will answer. With the conversation as the unit, neither follows. The next seat on the mission can answer the agent's port; your ask is not orphaned, it is open and goes into the next brief. The real ends are: answered, withdrawn by you, or stale by time, and staleness is a judgment at read time ("open since 3 October"), not a stored state change. What I built yesterday records a true fact, that the registry changed a session id, and the system-record mechanism is reusable. But the lapse and orphan readings of that fact should not reach the inbox as states. I would keep the outbox, stop treating a session change as closing anything, and let the brief carry open items forward. claude-15's fault-intake switch to reading the marks should not happen; I will tell them.

㊟ ("efficient accumulator") The kernel already answers "what is open as of now" from the act database, but it recomputes over the whole session on every turn, with a cap of ten thousand records. Over a conversation spanning sessions that cost grows, and the incremental form is a fold: each settled record updates a stored open set, standings and obligations for its conversation, which is what the hyperedge carrier in futon1b is for. The brief reads the accumulated state; the fold replaces both the per-turn recompute and the session-end act.

㊭ (order I would take) Mission id on the record, then the brief and its Emacs delivery, then run it on this REPL and on claude-15's, which have the longest histories, and count re-asks. Classifier after that, trained on the 1,540 incidences, feeding the brief's answered/kept distinction and then the kernel's effect rule. Session end demoted as above. If you agree I will write the first two packets; they are each one file.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what landed since you said "application led")
- Acts, standings, obligations, a typed ports status with a rules version, and the reply's own time are stored on every turn record. claude-15's follower reads them instead of running 象 code, so the spec's no-recomputation rule now holds on every seam.
- Session end is observable: the registry writes a durable outbox line on reset, deregister, reap or replaced id; the turn service turns it into a system record that lapses the agent's ports and marks yours orphaned or unread with the reason. Live since this evening; no session has ended yet, so the first such record is still to be seen.
- Tests caught one hazard: test suites had written nine fake session ends to the live outbox before the path was isolated; quarantined, fixed, never consumed.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (what the labelled data says about the kernel) Against the labellers, the kernel's links are 86% right as pairs but reach only 12% of the closes a reader sees. The candidate rule "only opener of its kind" would reach a third of the rest at 33% precision, so it is held. The current sole-port rule over-links asides 30% of the time, and every one of the 18 effect disagreements runs the same way: the kernel closes where a reader keeps. Batch 2 is the dataset to pick a tighter sole-port variant.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-16
previous_reply_acts.text: (one list still waiting on you, from the label consolidation) Proposals leaked into topics ("cheat-sheet", "bidding"), so for `propose` I recommend two cue-word moves, `tentative` ("I wonder if") and `directive` ("let's"), and no to the five topic labels; for `explain`, yes to `analogy`, `decision-rationale`, `consequence` and `mechanics` as an alias, no to `system-integration`. Yes or no per item, whenever.

previous_reply_acts.text: (nothing else needs you) Three small follow-ups are noted, not dispatched: an overlapping-turn edge in the reply-time window, the first real session-end record to verify, and the hyperedge loader once the vocabulary is closed.
